title: Round 34 Maryland-Delaware state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Maryland and Delaware. Every seeded row reproduces one USGS GNIS record screened by exact official name, returned type/state/county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and returned GNIS primary point, and cross-checked on two independent USGS surfaces (USGS GNIS Geocoder; staged-products DomesticNames text via tools/gnis_extract.py; cumulative candidate extract resources/city-subsurface/gnis-candidates-batch7.json with per-state ZIP SHA-256 values). Hoye-Crest carries a Domestic Names per-ID identity check. The Baltimore independent-city county naming, the Saint Mary's normalization, the Choptank parallel duplicate, and the Iron Hill / Ebright Azimuth decision are recorded below.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature and the point lay inside the intended state. County/census divisions, hundreds, historical places, military records, and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Second-surface cross-check of every seeded FEATURE_ID and per-ID identity checks for Hoye-Crest (1959484) and Iron Hill (214151), extracted in a GitHub Actions runner by tools/gnis_extract.py. The current text layout carries no elevation columns, so the summit elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values. The candidate extract file is cumulative across batches 7-16; this register is the frozen batch-16 evidence.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service, reproduced identically on the second USGS surface.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake for the accepted named lakes and reservoirs (text class Reservoir for Deep Creek Lake and Silver Lake; Lake for Lums Pond), Streams & Canals to Stream, and Summit to Summit.

A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit outline, or river centerline. Where GNIS carries a parallel duplicate record identical in name/class/county/point (Choptank River), the in-series record for the state is seeded and the duplicate is named in the identity decisions.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from that state gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

Maryland.title: Maryland statewide frame (Maryland-Delaware batch)
Maryland.frameNote: Maryland-Delaware batch: the Annapolis capital anchor is balanced with the per-ID Hoye-Crest high point (3,360 ft, seeded under its GNIS name because the Backbone Mountain record keys to West Virginia), Deep Creek Lake, and four river mouth records (Potomac, Susquehanna, Choptank, plus the corridor-held Pocomoke). Baltimore keeps its independent-city county identity (extract: Baltimore (city); Geocoder: City of Baltimore).

delaware.title: Delaware statewide frame (Maryland-Delaware batch)

Delaware is roughly 110 miles long; this is one of the narrowest frames in the atlas and its overview sits at the designed scale floor.

identityDecisions.candidate: Choptank River FEATURE_ID 583766 vs parallel duplicate 213797
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded 583766. Both records are identical in name, class (Stream), county (Dorchester), and primary point (38.6345644, -76.3266152) on both USGS surfaces; 583766 belongs to Maryland's original 58xxxx GNIS series while 213797 falls in Delaware's 21xxxx series and appears to be a later duplicate. As with the Guntersville Lake decision, one record is seeded and the twin is named, never silently merged.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Neither point is a channel centerline; the choice between identical records is an identification decision, not a survey.

identityDecisions.candidate: Baltimore county identity (extract Baltimore (city); Geocoder City of Baltimore)
identityDecisions.decision: Stored county is the extract's Baltimore (city); the register preserves the Geocoder's returned City of Baltimore verbatim in geocoderCounty. Stored coordinate is the GNIS populated place primary point.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The point is not a municipal boundary or address geocode.

identityDecisions.candidate: Potomac River county naming (extract St. Mary's; Geocoder Saint Mary's County)
identityDecisions.decision: Stored county is the extract's St. Mary's; the Geocoder's expanded Saint Mary's County is preserved in the register. This is the recurring generic Saint vs St. normalization, not two counties.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The point is the river's GNIS primary point at its Chesapeake mouth, not a centerline.

identityDecisions.decision: Backbone Mountain screened empty under states=MD (the ridge's GNIS record keys to West Virginia, whose frame already shipped). Maryland's high point on that ridge carries its own GNIS Summit record under the name Hoye-Crest (Garrett County), and that record is seeded with the per-ID check.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is the GNIS summit point, not a surveyed boundary marker.

identityDecisions.candidate: Ebright Azimuth (Delaware high point) under states=DE
identityDecisions.decision: Screened empty: the surveyed high point (447 ft) is a triangulation/azimuth station, and GNIS carries no Summit record for it. Delaware's starter register therefore seeds Iron Hill (214151), a named Summit reproduced by the per-ID check, and states the substitution openly rather than inventing a high-point row.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Iron Hill is not claimed to be the state high point; it is the highest-identity-safe GNIS Summit retained for the frame.

identityDecisions.candidate: Silver Lake same-name Delaware lakes (Kent 214647; New Castle 214649; Sussex 214646/214648)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the Kent County record 214647 (Dover's lake, identified by county and point); the three same-name lakes in New Castle/Sussex counties and the Silver Lake Manor/Shores communities are not seeded.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The seeded point is not a shoreline.

identityDecisions.decision: Screened empty under DE; the river's mouth record keys to Maryland. The Nanticoke remains a named context corridor in Delaware.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: Corridor treatment is not a claim that the river lacks a Delaware reach.

knownLimitations: Maryland and Delaware are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.

The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening by official name/type/state/county/FEATURE_ID is part of the evidence. Every seeded row was reproduced on the second USGS surface (staged-products DomesticNames text) at the same primary point.

The current DomesticNames text layout carries no elevation columns, so Hoye-Crest (3,360 feet) and Ebright Azimuth (447 feet) elevations cite USGS-published state-highpoint values; GNIS identity rests on the per-ID class/county/point reproduction.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain or corridors. Both frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context lines.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Both rectangles include Chesapeake/Delaware Bay waters and neighbouring-state land; no boundary geometry is claimed.
